policy_title: Fair Deal for Renters: Ban No-Fault Evictions and National Landlord Register
stated: Delivering a fair deal for renters by immediately banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies the default, and creating a national register of licensed landlords. Proactively enforcing clear standards for homes that are socially rented, including strict time limits for repairs.

source.quote: Delivering a fair deal for renters by immediately banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies the default, and creating a national register of licensed landlords. Proactively enforcing clear standards for homes that are socially rented, including strict time limits for repairs.

bearing_set.reason: Banning no-fault evictions, mandating three-year tenancy defaults, and creating a landlord register with repair standards directly affects security of tenure, affordability stability, and quality of rented housing stock — core affordable housing indicators.

Banning no-fault evictions and establishing default three-year tenancies materially strengthens renters' legal rights and due-process protections against arbitrary removal from their homes, a direct civil-rights effect.

A mandatory national landlord licensing register, compulsory minimum tenancy lengths as a default, and removal of landlords' no-fault eviction right impose new state licensing/mandate requirements and restrict property rights — a non-negligible worsening of O10 for a significant class of property owners.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O1 (the policy's designed target — tenure security and housing quality for renters) and O10 (the liberty/property-rights cost of compulsory licensing and constrained contracting for landlords). Effects on O14 (inequality) are real but route primarily through the tenure/housing mechanism captured in O1 rather than income distribution directly; O12 is not materially affected at the scale of a landlord register.
